title: Ordinary section localization over an ambient affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $F$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$. Let $S$ be open with underlying set the nonvanishing locus of $s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and let $U$ be affine open. There is an additive equivalence $e:Q^\Gamma(U)\simeq\Gamma(U\cap S,F)$ [def-sc-open-section-fraction-presentation] such that $s^n e([n,t])=t|_{U\cap S}$ for every $n\geq0$ and $t\in\Gamma(U,F\otimes L^{\otimes n})$. Multiplication is the section map of the inverse right unitor followed by tensorPowSection.

source.place: Tags 01PW (2), equation module-invert-s, and 09MR, affine-open paragraph

proof.text: Restrict L and F to U.toScheme and take the ordinary restricted global section sU. Use restrictFunctorIsoPullback and IsInvertible.of_iso to obtain invertibility; quasi-coherence is the Mathlib restriction instance. Invoke the tensor-power section comparison to obtain numerator equivalences N and transition compatibility.

Prove privately that the additive closure of the fraction generators is the underlying additive subgroup of their module span: the generators are stable under scalar multiplication by Hom.app_smul and DirectSum.of_smul; the closure is consequently a submodule. Form the direct-sum equivalence from N. Its image carries the generators bijectively to the restricted generators by transition compatibility, using the inverse N in the reverse direction. AddMonoidHom.map_closure and QuotientAddGroup.congr descend it to Q, with the generator formula hQ.

Apply affine_section_localization to the affine scheme U.toScheme and restricted data. Its nonvanishing open V equals the preimage of S, by nonvanishingLocus_restrict and hS. The image-preimage identity of an open immersion therefore identifies its image with U intersection S.

Obtain T on the image of V from the tensor-power section comparison. Compose Q, the affine localization equivalence e, and T. For each numerator t, rewrite Q([n,t]) by hQ, apply the affine tensor formula to N(n)(t), and use the forward implication in the coefficient comparison. This proves the original formula without changing its signature or imposing nonempty/nonzero assumptions.

lean.statement: theorem affineOpen_sectionFraction_localization (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (S : X.Opens) (hS : (S : Set X) = nonvanishingLocus L s) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : ∃ e : OpenSectionFractionPresentation L F s U ≃+ Γ(F, U ⊓ S), ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : Γ(F ⊗ L.tensorPow n, U)), (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) : F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : X.Modules)).app (U ⊓ S) (e (openSectionFraction L F s U n t)) = (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U ⊓ S ≤ U)).op t
